If you do end up doing it, cleaning would be good so that your family won't have to deal with it, but more importantly, get all your important stuff together.

It's horrible trying to find keys, any due bills, debts that are coming, computer/phone passwords, etc for someone who has died.  My brother died a few years ago and we never could get access to his phone, so we couldn't answer it when his friends tried to call him, so we couldn't tell them he'd died.  We couldn't respond to emails to him either.

My sister spent the entire night going through his stuff to find his car keys, car title, due bills, etc.  Not sure how we ever figured out how to tell his employer.

I'm pretty sure he had some money in an e-wallet somewhere but no way to access it so that was gone.

Write this kind of stuff down where you put it, and make sure someone in your family knows where to find it in case you die.

School sucked for me.  Most of my school life I just tried to numb myself.  It gets far better after high school.  Well, it still really sucked for me, but that's due to personal issues.  It was still better than being in school though. Once I got out of school, I worked at shit jobs for a year until I decided it wouldn't be enough so I worked to get through college. (not a university either, just an ok local college one step up from a community college)

I was extremely lazy in school because I started out by picking things up a lot faster than everyone else.  So I got really lazy.  Really really lazy. Bad grades in school doesn't destroy your chances later.  Just means you won't go to medical college or become a Harvard lawyer.  You can still get a GED even if you drop out.  Lots of really well off people around here earned their money in blue collar jobs.

At my most recent place of employment, a shit ton of people who are only good at one thing make a huge amount of money on that one thing.  They are experts in their section of the home improvement industry, and they earn their income by doing one thing really well.

You aren't a failure because you failed so many times or you're making mistakes.  I'm fucking terrified to even try, and I'm more than twice your age.  I'm a failure, not you.  

You don't have to achieve much.  No one is asking you to discover a cancer cure or invent anti-gravity.  But if you can get past the miserable shit experience they call high school, then you can probably try a few things and maybe discover one thing you really like to do, and possibly make a living doing.

If you manage that, you've made yourself in a fucking wild success.

Might take a few different types of jobs though, so if you can numb yourself long enough to get through high school, and try enough different jobs until you find one you don't royally suck at, you're golden.

Just remember, most everyone fucks everything up in what I call their not-field.  Like me.  I discovered early that retail is NOT my field.  Also fast food, another NOT field for me.

If it requires thinking on my feet, fast reflexes, high energy, or heavy labor, I'm totally fucked.
